hints: Focus on what complete combustion means here, each element forming its normal stable oxide.
Write the formula of each oxide first, for example sodium forms $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ while magnesium forms $\text{MgO}$.
Balance each equation for $\text{O}_2$ and then divide by the moles of element to find moles of $\text{O}_2$ needed per 1 mol of atoms, then pick the smallest.
walkthrough:
**Recall the stable oxide for each element**

Think of the group number and charge. Group 1 makes +1, Group 2 makes +2, and so on.

$\text{Na} \to \text{Na}_2\text{O}$, $\text{Mg} \to \text{MgO}$, $\text{Al} \to \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{P} \to \text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$

**Write balanced equations with oxygen**

Now balance each one with $\text{O}_2$ as the other reactant.

$$4\text{Na} + \text{O}_2 \to 2\text{Na}_2\text{O}$$
$$2\text{Mg} + \text{O}_2 \to 2\text{MgO}$$
$$4\text{Al} + 3\text{O}_2 \to 2\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$$
$$4\text{P} + 5\text{O}_2 \to \text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$$

**Calculate moles of oxygen per 1 mol of atoms**

Divide moles of $\text{O}_2$ by moles of element in the balanced equation.

For $\text{Na}$: $1/4 = 0.25$ mol $\text{O}_2$

For $\text{Mg}$: $1/2 = 0.50$ mol $\text{O}_2$

For $\text{Al}$: $3/4 = 0.75$ mol $\text{O}_2$

For $\text{P}$: $5/4 = 1.25$ mol $\text{O}_2$

**Pick the smallest value**

Comparing 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 and 1.25, the smallest is 0.25. That belongs to sodium, which needs only one $\text{O}$ atom for every two $\text{Na}$ atoms.

options.A: Aluminium forms $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$. The equation $4\text{Al} + 3\text{O}_2 \to 2\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ needs 0.75 mol $\text{O}_2$ per 1 mol Al. This is more than sodium because Al is +3 and needs more oxygen.
options.B: Magnesium forms $\text{MgO}$. The equation $2\text{Mg} + \text{O}_2 \to 2\text{MgO}$ needs 0.50 mol $\text{O}_2$ per 1 mol Mg. This is twice as much as sodium, so it is not the least.
options.C: Phosphorus undergoes complete combustion to $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$. The equation $4\text{P} + 5\text{O}_2 \to \text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ needs 1.25 mol $\text{O}_2$ per 1 mol P. This is the largest value, as P is in oxidation state +5.
options.D: Sodium forms $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$. The equation $4\text{Na} + \text{O}_2 \to 2\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ needs only 0.25 mol $\text{O}_2$ per 1 mol Na. Because Na is +1, two Na atoms share one O atom, giving the lowest oxygen demand.
